title: A linear system containing ideal products is immersive
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a $k$-scheme, $i:Z\to Y$ a closed immersion, $\mathcal I$ its ideal, and $L$ an invertible module. Schemes, closed immersions, ideals and invertible modules are as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $r\le n$ be natural numbers, assume $L^{\otimes r}$ is very ample [def-sc-ample], and let $\sigma$ be global generating sections [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] of $\mathcal I\otimes L^{\otimes(n-r)}$. Put $U=Y\setminus i(Z)$. Let $A$ be a finite index type and let $s_a\in\Gamma(Y,L^{\otimes n})$ be sections whose $k$-linear span contains every section restricting to zero on $Z$. Suppose their pullbacks $t_a$ generate $L^{\otimes n}|_U$. Then the morphism $U\to\mathbf P(A;k)$ classified by the $t_a$ [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections] is an immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].

source.place: Tag 0FD5, lemma-generate-over-complement, product-of-sections argument in the proof

proof.text: Choose a closed immersion $j:Y\to\mathbf P(B;k)$ with $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L^{\otimes r}$ from very ampleness. Pull its coordinate sections back to sections $t_b$; their nonvanishing loci cover $Y$.

At $x\in U$, restriction of the ideal inclusion is an isomorphism. Hence the images of the given ideal-twist generators generate $L^{\otimes(n-r)}$ at $x$. Choose such an image $a$ nonvanishing at $x$, and choose $t_b$ nonvanishing at $x$. The products $a\otimes t_c$, transported through $L^{\otimes(n-r)}\otimes L^{\otimes r}\cong L^{\otimes n}$, vanish on $Z$. The tensor fibre formula says that the nonvanishing locus of $a\otimes t_b$ is the intersection of the two nonvanishing loci. It lies in $U$.

Every product is a constant linear combination of the specified $s_a$ by the span assumption. On the projective target, divide these linear forms by one coordinate and invert the form corresponding to $a\otimes t_b$. The ratios $(a\otimes t_c)/(a\otimes t_b)$ then define a morphism to the $b$-th standard affine chart of $\mathbf P(B;k)$. Construct it from the polynomial coordinate ring. The coordinate formulas for a generating system identify its inverse image with the nonvanishing locus of $a\otimes t_b$.

On this inverse image, both tensor factors are generators. Trivialize by them: the pulled-back ratios cancel the first factor and equal $t_c/t_b$. Maps into the affine chart are determined by the base functions and these ratios, so the composite with the constructed chart morphism equals the restriction of $j$. That restriction is an immersion. Immersion cancellation proves that the specified coordinate morphism is an immersion over this target open.

These target opens cover the image, since a product nonvanishing at each $x\in U$ was chosen. Apply locality near the image. If $U$ is empty, the same image-cover argument is vacuous and gives the assertion.
